title: Compose the scheduler release kernel so a lease can durably reach RELEASED
description:
Objective: make `leaseState === "RELEASED"` reachable in durable daemon state by composing the release authority that already exists, and retire the daemon's duplicate of a design-765 rule that it never should have owned.

TWO MEASURED FACTS, both at HEAD a42ae2f.

FACT 1 — THE KERNEL EXISTS AND NOTHING CALLS IT. `releaseWork` at `packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:194` IS the design-765 release authority. It fences authority, treats an already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease as `NO_OP`, refuses a malformed request or an uncommittable handoff BEFORE composing any transition, and then splits three ways on `safeBoundaryObserved && effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal`: unsettled returns `outcome: "DRAINING"` with the lease at `DRAINING` and `resumable: false`; settled returns `outcome: "RELEASED"` with `lease.state === "RELEASED"`, the parsed `ReleaseHandoff`, the composed `DrainDisposition` and `resumable: disposition.resumable`. `grep -rn "releaseWork" apps` returns ZERO callers.

FACT 2 — THE SCHEDULER ROOT PUBLISHES NONE OF IT. A compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon importing from `@moe/scheduler`, typechecked and deleted in one command, returned errors for EVERY release symbol: TS2724 for `LEASE_STATES` ("Did you mean 'LeaseState'?") and TS2305 for `releaseWork`, `applyDrainReason`, `parseDisposition`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest` and `ReleaseResult`. `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:109` exports `SLOT_STATES` and the `LeaseState` type and nothing else from this family. A root-barrel grep is not evidence here; re-run the probe.

WHY THIS IS ALSO A CORRECTION, NOT ONLY AN ADDITION. task-740924b7 landed `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts` (249 lines, DONE and QA-approved) which validates a drain disposition through `@moe/runner`'s `parseDrainDisposition` / `isMonotonicDisposition` and then DERIVES `resumable` itself at :170 via a local `isResumable(disposition)`. That was correct against the surface available at the time and its values agree with the scheduler's today — but `@moe/scheduler`'s `DrainDisposition` (lease-drain.ts:31-38) ALREADY CARRIES `resumable`, computed by `composeDisposition` under the design-765 comment "only an unchanged strongest `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` stays resumable". The daemon now holds a second definition of that rule. The module's own header warns of exactly this: "two definitions would drift and core's release predicate would start refusing silently." Note also that the runner's `DrainDisposition` has NO `resumable` member while the scheduler's does, and core's `ExpansionReleaseEvidence.disposition` is `{resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget}` — the scheduler's shape, not the runner's.

Deliverable, in order: (1) publish the release family from `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts`; (2) call `releaseWork` from the daemon's attempt release path; (3) persist its `ReleaseResult` onto the existing durable row so `leaseState` carries the kernel's answer instead of the activation-time snapshot; (4) delete the local `isResumable` and take `resumable` from the returned disposition.

NOT in scope: the provider-slot release transition (task-4731ba34 — `releaseWork` does not touch slots), the terminal effect/resource refs, the safe-boundary observation, the `{digest, ref}` handoff projection (task-af9454f4, whose durable source is now this task's `ReleaseHandoff`), or the evidence reader (task-e62e3828).

Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/index.ts, apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts and its test, and the daemon call site.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — four legs, exit codes captured SEPARATELY, and read each `Test Files N passed` count line rather than the exit code.
definitionOfDone: The release family is reachable from the `@moe/scheduler` package ROOT: the same compiled bare-specifier probe that returned TS2305/TS2724 for `releaseWork`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest`, `ReleaseResult`, `applyDrainReason` and `parseDisposition` now typechecks clean, and the probe is deleted in the same command. Record the before and after output.

A lease durably reaches `RELEASED`: an end-to-end test drives the daemon release path with a settled boundary and reads `leaseState === "RELEASED"` back FROM DURABLE BYTES, where before this task the recorded value was the activation-time `ACTIVE` and `RELEASED` was unreachable.

The DRAINING branch is proven separately and is not collapsed into the released one: with `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` or `resourcesTerminal` false, the durable row records the DRAINING outcome and `resumable: false`, and a test asserts it differs from the released row field by field.

`resumable` comes from the kernel, not from the daemon: the local `isResumable` helper is DELETED, `grep -rn "isResumable" apps/daemon/src` returns zero, and the recorded value is the `disposition.resumable` the scheduler returned.
An already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease records the kernel's `NO_OP` outcome rather than a refusal or a second release row, and a test pins that a replay leaves exactly one durable row.

A mutation that makes the daemon derive `resumable` locally again, and separately one that records the activation-time lease state instead of the kernel's, each turn a NAMED test red; record both test names.

All four gate legs run with exit codes captured separately, both test legs print a nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Depends on the boundary and terminal facts: `releaseWork`'s ReleaseRequest requires `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal`, which are task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781. Until those land, drive them from the test as INPUTS to the kernel; never let the daemon assert them as durable truth on its own.
No caller-supplied lease state, disposition, truth class or handoff may become authority. The kernel decides; the daemon persists what it decided. Missing or unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN.
Use public package roots across package boundaries; the first step is the root export, not a deep import. Widen `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` only by the symbols this task actually consumes.

Exact codes and layers on every refusal path, positive generated counts on any sweep, target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400. attempt-release-disposition.ts is at 249 today, so this task must split it rather than grow it.

(c) NO_OP: "answers the kernel's NO_OP on replay and leaves EXACTLY ONE durable row". Rows are counted OUT OF THE STORE by a `durableRowCount` helper that filters the raw event stream, not inferred from a return value. The replay uses a DIFFERENT reason (WORK_CANCEL) so a second row would be observable, and asserts the surviving row still reads WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE / RELEASED / RELEASED. The REVOKED arm of NO_OP is unreachable from this daemon path — `releaseWork` sets the settled lease to RELEASED whatever the terminal target — so it is driven at the scheduler root instead, in step 1's "answers NO_OP for a lease the root release authority already terminated".

(d) resumable comes from the kernel, and the drill that must catch a re-derivation is NON-EQUIVALENT. The row carries BOTH values because the kernel returns both and they legitimately disagree: `disposition.resumable` is what design 765 says about the reason set, and top-level `resumable` is `ReleaseResult.resumable`, what THIS release permits. On a DRAINING row with reason WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE the test asserts `disposition.resumable === true` AND `resumable === false`. A caller-supplied `resumable` that contradicts the composed one is refused outright by `parseDisposition`, covered by "carries the KERNEL's refusal for a DOWNGRADED strongest reason".

implementationPlan.description: Wire `releaseWork` and retire the daemon's duplicate rule. In `attempt-release-disposition.ts`, build the `AuthorityProof` `releaseWork` fences against — `{leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, expectedVersion, authorityHashRef}` — entirely from the RE-READ committed activation's `record.lease`, which carries every one of those fields; a caller-supplied proof is never consulted. Pass the `ReleaseRequest` through and let the kernel decide: it already runs `applyDrainReason(parsed.disposition, parsed.reason)` internally, so the daemon stops parsing or judging the disposition itself. DELETE the local `isResumable` at :158 and take `resumable` from the returned `disposition` — `grep -rn "isResumable" apps/daemon/src` must return zero. WATCH FOR A NEWLY UNREACHABLE CODE, which is the real hazard of this step: once the daemon no longer calls `@moe/runner`'s `parseDrainDisposition` / `isMonotonicDisposition`, any member of the frozen `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_CODES` that only that path could raise becomes unreachable while its test keeps passing against a hand-built input. For each code, either carry the kernel's own rejection (its `issues[0].code` and `.message`, surfaced unchanged) or REMOVE the code from the frozen list and from the vocabulary test in the same commit. Do not leave a dead member. Leave the runner-surface exports that task-740924b7 added in place; they are simply no longer imported here.
implementationPlan.note:
`releaseWork` is wired and the daemon's duplicate of design 765 is gone.

PROOF FROM DURABLE BYTES ONLY. `proofOf(lease)` builds all five AuthorityProof fields — leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, expectedVersion, authorityHashRef — off the lease itself; there is no caller channel for a proof. ONE DELIBERATE STRENGTHENING of the step text: the lease handed to the kernel is the one the KERNEL last answered, read back out of the durable release row via the root's own `parseLeaseRecord`, falling back to the committed activation's `record.lease` only when no release row exists. Fencing a replay against the activation-time snapshot would make `releaseWork`'s NO_OP branch unreachable from this path forever — the activation lease is pinned ACTIVE by `claimWork`'s CLAIM_LEGAL_LEASE_STATES = ["ACTIVE"] — and DoD 5 requires exactly that branch. The full LeaseRecord is therefore persisted on the row and `leaseState` is its projection; a test pins `row.leaseState === row.lease.state` so the flat field cannot drift from the record it projects. Any prior-row refusal other than RECORD_ABSENT aborts rather than falling back, so an unreadable history can never be released over.

`isResumable` DELETED. `grep -rn "isResumable" apps/daemon/src` -> exit 1, zero hits. Positive control on that empty grep: `grep -rln "isResumable" --include=*.ts .` still finds packages/runner/src/recovery/recovery-contract.ts and safe-boundary.ts, so the grep works and the absence is real. `grep -rn "parseDrainDisposition\|isMonotonicDisposition\|DRAIN_TERMINAL_TARGETS" apps/daemon/src/work/` -> zero. The runner-surface exports task-740924b7 added are left in place: `git diff --numstat 8557296..HEAD -- packages/runner/src/` is empty.

NO DEAD MEMBER IN THE FROZEN LIST. Five codes were retired WITH the validator that raised them (REASON_UNKNOWN, REASON_NOT_UNIONED, DISPOSITION_MALFORMED, DISPOSITION_DOWNGRADED, TARGET_MISMATCH); the vocabulary test asserts each is ABSENT by name, so a silent re-add reddens. Their refusals are now carried verbatim — `issues[0].code` and `.message` unchanged — under the new SCHEDULER_LEASE_DRAIN layer, which has no `_LAYER` suffix and so does not enter the security-boundary roster scan (matching the sibling DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT).

Each of the seven SURVIVING codes was then audited for a real DRIVING path, not a hand-built input, and three were missing one, so three cases were added:
- COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE was the code most at risk of going dead, because the replay path now answers NO_OP instead of failing the commit. "refuses a SECOND transition over a DRAINING row rather than appending one" drives it honestly: DRAINING is not terminal, so the kernel composes a real RELEASED transition on the second call and the expectedVersion-0 aggregate has nowhere to put it. Refused, one row, still DRAINING. (The durable DRAINING -> RELEASED progression needs a versioned aggregate and is out of this task's scope; refusing is the honest behaviour, not a fabricated success.)
- RECORD_DRIFT gained "refuses to fence against a stored lease the scheduler's parser will not accept" — a planted, canonically-encoded row with a declared outcome so the byte compare and the outcome guard both pass and ONLY the lease parse can refuse. This is the guard a corrupted lease would otherwise slip past into the kernel.
- RECORD_UNREADABLE gained "refuses an UNREADABLE store separately from an absent row", driven by closing the real store handle.
Per-code assertion counts in the test file, all non-zero: BINDING_MISMATCH 2, ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE 3, COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE 2, RECORD_ABSENT 4, RECORD_AMBIGUOUS 2, RECORD_DRIFT 4, RECORD_UNREADABLE 2.

implementationPlan.description: Feed the boundary facts as INPUTS, never as daemon-asserted truth, and keep the call site honest. `releaseWork`'s `ReleaseRequest` requires `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal`, whose durable producers are task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781 and are NOT landed — both are BLOCKED. Until they land, those three arrive on the request and the daemon passes them through to the kernel unmodified; it must never synthesize, default, or optimistically upgrade any of them, and it must not record them as durable truth of its own. THE PROOF IS CONSTRUCTIBLE FROM DURABLE BYTES, which is what makes this composition legal. `parseProof` (lease-fencing.ts:51) requires `{leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, expectedVersion, authorityHashRef}`. `LeaseRecord` (authority-kernel.ts:83-95) carries leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, authorityHashRef, state and version. 1. THE NEWLY UNREACHABLE REFUSAL CODE. Once the daemon stops calling the runner's disposition validators, any member of the frozen `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_CODES` that only that path could raise is dead - and its test keeps passing, because the test hands the refusal helper a hand-built input rather than driving production into that state. A dead code in a frozen list is worse than no code: it reads as coverage.

THE THREE BOUNDARY FLAGS ARE NOT PROVEN FACTS YET. `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal` have no durable producer - task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781 are both BLOCKED, each on further prerequisites. 5. Both roster-guard files live nowhere near the code being changed; a worker who bumps the count but not the sorted list gets an array-diff failure that reads like an unrelated regression.

7. attempt-release-disposition.ts has ONE line of headroom against the 250 target. Any step that adds before the split has already broken the cap.
